name: Analyse equipment condition and failures
summary: Reliability engineers turn failures and condition data into changes that prevent the next failure. Each case starts from a forced outage report, an outage as-found report, a bad-actor list or a scheduled review; significant failures get a formal root cause analysis with site evidence, trend data and sometimes a lab report, and the rest get a work-history and condition review. Findings go through a monthly review with plant maintenance and an asset manager's approval, and end as a maintenance strategy change, a spares change or a capital candidate. Cases are slow because lab reports take weeks, reviews wait for the monthly meeting and site visits need travel and permits.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with about 1,300 staff, three gas steam units converted from coal at the Wabamun-area sites, two cogeneration plants, 17 hydro plants and 12 wind farms, with a central engineering and asset management division of about 130 people.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019 to 2022. Cycling of the converted units after 2020-2021 changed failure patterns and added work.

trigger: A forced outage condition report, an outage as-found report, a bad-actor list or a scheduled strategy review reaches a reliability engineer.
end_state: A maintenance strategy or spares change is issued, a capital candidate is sent to capital planning, or the case is closed with no change.

volume.seasonality: More cases after the spring and fall outage seasons, when as-found reports arrive.

evidence.note: Kept from the organisation file; about two cases a month per reliability engineer is consistent with 14 reliability engineers and 9 electrical engineers who also support outages and projects.

surge.cause: as-found reports after the spring and fall outage seasons

evidence.note: Author's estimate: outage condition reports arrive in the weeks after each outage season.
14 reliability engineers; the rest of their time goes to outage scoping, capital planning and condition reports.
Electrical and protection reviews.
Approvals and capital write-ups.
Keys maintenance plan changes; not listed in the organisation file's roles for this process.

systems.name: ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Hydro, wind and battery SCADA and remote control
Document management and engineering drawings repository

steps.name: Log the trigger in the reliability tracker
steps.description: The reliability engineer for the fleet area logs the trigger (a forced outage condition report, an outage as-found report, a monthly bad-actor list, a condition monitoring alert or a scheduled strategy review) in the reliability tracking spreadsheet with the equipment ID, work order numbers, date and owner.

evidence.note: A tracking database of failures with work order numbers, owners and dates (ml_rca).

steps.name: Decide whether a root cause analysis is needed
steps.description: The reliability engineer applies the triggers in the reliability procedure: did the failure cause a unit trip or derate, did critical equipment fail, did a component fail before its expected life, or is it a repeat failure. Significant failures get a formal root cause analysis; the rest get a condition or work-history review.

error.defect_description: A significant failure screened out as routine and later repeats.

evidence.note: RCA triggers: failure before set service life and failure of critical equipment (ml_rca); the 30 percent share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel to the plant or wind site
steps.description: The reliability engineer drives a company truck from the engineering office to the plant, hydro site or wind farm where the failure happened, often two to four hours each way for southern Alberta wind farms and the Bow River plants.

evidence.note: Engineering office in Calgary or Edmonton; driving times to Wabamun, Bow River and southern Alberta wind sites estimated.

steps.name: Collect evidence and interview staff
steps.description: On site the engineer examines and photographs the failed parts, collects samples (oil, debris, fractured pieces), and interviews the operators, mechanics and electricians who were there, under the permit for the isolated equipment. Wind turbine nacelles can only be reached when wind speed is below the climbing limit.

control.basis: Permit to work and lockout before inspecting isolated equipment (Alberta OHS Code Part 15)

evidence.note: Evidence collection by interviews and inspection of failed parts (ml_rca); isolation before inspection (ohs15); hours estimated.

steps.name: Pull trends, alarms and work order history
steps.description: Back at the office the engineer exports historian trends and DCS or SCADA alarm logs for the hours before the failure, and pulls the work order history for the asset from the ERP, looking for earlier symptoms, recent maintenance and repeat failures.

next.condition: parts sent for lab or OEM analysis

evidence.note: Review of failure history and past fixes (ml_rca).

steps.name: Wait for lab or OEM failure analysis
steps.description: Failed parts or oil samples go to a metallurgical lab or the OEM, which returns a report on the failure mode (fatigue, creep, corrosion, lubrication loss) after several weeks.

evidence.note: Turnaround of metallurgical and OEM failure analyses estimated at two to eight weeks.

steps.name: Run the root cause analysis session
steps.description: The reliability engineer leads a session with operations, maintenance and the OEM representative, builds a cause-and-effect or five-whys chart from the evidence and agrees the physical, human and organisational causes.

error.defect_description: Symptom recorded as the root cause, so the corrective action does not stop the failure.

evidence.note: Complex failures are analysed by a cross-functional team led by the reliability engineer (rew2008); hours estimated.

steps.name: Review electrical and protection data
steps.description: The electrical and protection engineer reviews relay event records, generator and transformer test data (dissolved gas, insulation resistance, partial discharge) and protection settings to confirm or rule out electrical causes.

evidence.note: Electrical engineers in the asset management team review protection and test data; hours estimated.

steps.name: Draft the root cause report and corrective actions
steps.description: The reliability engineer writes the report in plain language: equipment, failure dates, history, evidence, root causes and proposed corrective actions with owners and dates, with captioned photos and trend plots.

evidence.note: Report contents per ml_rca; hours estimated.

steps.name: Analyse work order history and condition data
steps.description: For a review the engineer pulls 12 to 36 months of work orders and condition data for the asset class, ranks bad actors by number of repair and emergency work orders, lost generation and cost, and looks for patterns such as failures after starts, which became more common when converted units began cycling.

error.defect_description: Work orders coded to the wrong asset or failure code skew the ranking.

evidence.note: Ranking the 15 assets with most repair and emergency work orders and narrowing to 10 by production loss, safety and cost (rew2008).

steps.name: Review electrical test results
steps.description: The electrical engineer reviews oil analysis, thermography and offline test trends for the transformers, generators, breakers or wind turbine converters in the review and grades each asset's condition.

evidence.note: Condition assessment of electrical assets is common practice; hours estimated.

steps.name: Draft recommendation
steps.description: The reliability engineer writes the recommendation: change a preventive maintenance task or interval, add condition monitoring, change spare-part stock, or propose a capital replacement, with the expected reduction in failures and cost.

evidence.note: Common practice; hours estimated.

steps.name: Review findings with plant maintenance
steps.description: At the monthly reliability meeting the engineer presents the report or recommendation to plant managers, maintenance supervisors, planners and technicians, who challenge the causes and actions and agree owners and dates or send it back for more work.

evidence.note: Review meeting of 10 to 20 managers, engineers, supervisors and technicians to reach a group decision (ml_rca); a monthly cadence is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve actions and funding
steps.description: The asset manager reviews the agreed actions against the maintenance budget and risk, approves strategy and spares changes, sends capital-sized items to capital planning and closes recommendations that are not worth doing.

control.basis: Maintenance budget and asset management decision authority

evidence.note: Branch shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update maintenance plans in the ERP
steps.description: A maintenance planner edits the task lists and maintenance plans in the ERP plant maintenance module: new or changed tasks, intervals, crafts and parts, and reschedules the next due dates for every affected asset at each site.

error.defect_description: Interval or task applied to the wrong functional locations.

evidence.note: Maintenance plan changes are keyed by planners; hours estimated.

steps.name: Tell sites about the strategy change
steps.description: The reliability engineer sends the revised strategy to the plant, hydro and wind maintenance supervisors with the reasons and the date it takes effect, and updates the maintenance strategy document in the document store.

evidence.note: The organisation file sends maintenance strategies to gas, hydro and wind maintenance.

steps.name: Change spare-part stocking levels
steps.description: The reliability engineer raises a material master change asking supply chain to add a critical spare or change minimum and maximum stock, with the failure history and lead time as justification, and follows up until stores confirms it.

evidence.note: Critical spares policy is part of the process description in the organisation file; hours estimated.

steps.name: Write the asset condition report for capital planning
steps.description: The asset manager writes up the asset's condition, failure history, risk and remaining life with a rough replacement cost, and adds it to the list of candidates for the next capital plan.

evidence.note: The organisation file links this process to capital planning through the condition report.

exceptions.name: Lab or OEM failure analysis
exceptions.description: Failed parts go to a lab or the OEM and the analysis waits weeks for the report.

exceptions.name: Sent back at the review meeting
exceptions.description: Plant maintenance does not accept the causes or actions and the engineer revises the recommendation for the next meeting.

exceptions.name: No change justified
exceptions.description: The asset manager closes the case because the change is not worth its cost.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trigger to issued change
benchmarks.population: Reliability cases at an Alberta generator, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: reviews close within about two monthly meeting cycles once queue time is counted; root cause analyses with lab work take two to four months.
15 assets with most repair and emergency work orders narrowed to 10.
10 to 20 individuals; mode is the author's midpoint.

pain_points.description: Work orders are often closed without good failure codes or notes, so ranking bad actors from ERP history needs manual cleaning.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common CMMS data quality in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Lab and OEM failure analyses take weeks and hold the root cause report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Findings wait for the monthly review meeting, and rejected recommendations wait a further month.

evidence.note: Group review meeting before decision.

pain_points.description: Strategy changes are re-keyed into ERP maintenance plans site by site, and some are applied to the wrong assets.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

assumptions: Shares of trigger sources are the author's estimate; the organisation file lists only forced outage reports as a trigger and work order history and outage condition reports as inputs.
Corrective action effectiveness checks six to twelve months later are part of the ongoing program and are not in the simulated cycle.
Spare-part stocking changes are sent to scm-manage-stores as a material request; the organisation file has no link for this.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).

sources.title: Root Cause Analysis - A Practical Guide (J. Martinez)
sources.supports: RCA triggers (failure before a set service life, failure of critical equipment); a tracking database of failures with work order numbers and owners; evidence collection by interviewing operators and inspecting failed parts; plain-language report with root cause, history, solution and owner; review meeting of 10 to 20 managers, engineers, supervisors and technicians; a reliability engineer tracks actions and follow-up.

sources.title: Targeting Bad Actors to Pass the Generation Uptime Test (D. Abecunas)
sources.supports: Bad-actor program at generating plants: the reliability engineer pulls the 15 assets with the most repair and emergency work orders from the asset management system and narrows them to 10 by production loss, safety and cost; simple failures are analysed by the engineer alone and complex ones by a cross-functional team; the program is kept up with quarterly updates.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 15 Managing the Control of Hazardous Energy (Alberta Regulation 191/2021)
sources.supports: Part 15 requires isolation of machinery and equipment before work (s. 212), verification of isolation (s. 213), personal locks (s. 214) and rules for securing by individual workers and groups. The same Part existed in the earlier Code (AR 87/2009) in force in 2019 to 2021.
